source_text: Ταῦτα (λέξεις τινὰς) εὑρὼν ἔν τινι συγγράμματι αὐτῶν ἐνισταμένων τῷ Μιλτιάδου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ συγγράμματι, ἐν ᾧ ἀποδείκνυσι περὶ τοῦ μὴ δεῖν προφήτην ἐν ἐκστάσει λαλεῖν, ἐπετεμόμην.
thought_title: The author's source for the Miltiades argument
orientation: The author is explaining where he found the argument he has just quoted, namely in a writing of theirs that opposed Miltiades' work.
pass_a_gloss: These things (certain words) I found in some writing of theirs, of those opposing the writing of Miltiades the brother, in which he demonstrates concerning the not needing a prophet to speak in ecstasy, I excerpted.

choices.why: The participle describes the Montanists as actively resisting or standing against Miltiades' writing; 'opposing' captures the adversarial stance.
The middle voice of ἐπιτέμνω means to cut out or excerpt for oneself; 'I excerpted' preserves the author's act of selecting the passage.
The glossary requires 'ecstasy' for this term, and the context is the prophetic state Miltiades argued against.
The genitive phrase identifies Miltiades as 'the brother,' a title of respect or familiarity; keeping it literal preserves the source's designation.

pass_b_english: I found these words in a writing of theirs, in which they oppose the writing of Miltiades, a fellow Christian. In that writing Miltiades demonstrates that a prophet must not speak in ecstasy. I excerpted these words from it.

polish.changed: Clarified that 'the brother' means a fellow Christian, split the long sentence into two for easier reading, and made the sequence of actions clearer.

notes.why: Unclear if 'brother' means fellow Christian, literal sibling, or something else.
notes.fix: Note: 'brother' = fellow Christian writer, not biological sibling.

notes.why: 'The brother' is an unexplained title; reader may think it means a sibling.
notes.fix: Explain 'brother' means fellow Christian, not a literal sibling.
